title: The beautiful factors
hookLine: faith, mindfulness, conscience, concern, non-greed, non-hate, balance

cards: The manual could have called them the good factors. It calls them the beautiful ones, sobhana.
All week this path has been naming what troubles a moment of mind: the four under every unwholesome moment, greed's family, aversion's family, dullness and doubt. A long list, and an honest one.
Today the week closes by turning the cloth over, and the manual's other side begins with seven.

teach.b: First, faith, saddha. In the Questions of King Milinda, Nagasena gives faith a picture. A king's army crosses a stream and churns it to mud.
The king is thirsty. A water-clearing gem is dropped in, the mud settles, and the water is fit to drink. Faith, in that picture, is less about believing hard and more about the mind settling clear.
Second, mindfulness, sati: the mind that doesn't float off, that stays with what's here. Third and fourth come as a pair.
Conscience, hiri: the inner pull of, this is beneath me. Concern, ottappa: care for what an act will do. The troubled four included shamelessness and recklessness; these are their exact opposites.
In the Anguttara Nikaya, the Buddha calls this pair two bright qualities that protect the world. Then non-greed, alobha: the open hand. Non-hate, adosa: the friendly face that doesn't turn away.
And balance, tatramajjhattata: evenness, a mind holding things without tipping. These seven, with tomorrow's six pairs, the manual finds in every beautiful moment of mind.

teach.h: AN OPEN HAND, A FRIENDLY FACE.
teach.b: They aren't rare peak experiences: a settled mind, a mind that stays, some self-respect, some care, an open hand, a friendly face, an even keel.
The Dhammapada sums up the teaching in one verse, in Max Müller's words: "Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened."
The beautiful factors are what that purifying looks like from inside, one moment at a time. A moment can be colored by greed, envy, fog, or by faith, care and an open hand.
The same knowing, a different dye.

how: Abhidhamma students learn the beautiful factors by their Pali names alongside the unwholesome ones, and some Theravada teachers call hiri and ottappa, conscience and concern, the guardians of the world.

o: the gold paint used on temple statues
a blessing a monk gives at a festival
the factors that color a moment of mind well

p: faith: the gem that clears the water
concern: care for what an act will do

s: the manual calls these 'the good factors'
it calls them sobhana, the beautiful.
conscience and concern are exact opposites of shamelessness and recklessness
the troubled four held the shadows; these are the light.
in Nagasena's picture, faith means believing without looking
he compares faith to a gem that clears muddy water so the king can drink.

games.q: you're the king. your army has churned the stream to mud, and you're thirsty. what clears the water?
o: wait a day for it to settle.
games.why: in Nagasena's picture, the gem goes in and the mud settles. faith, he says, works like that in the mind.

practice: If you'd like, look for something beautiful in this moment, in the manual's sense: mindfulness, the mind staying with the breath; balance, a little evenness; or non-hate, someone comes to mind and the face doesn't turn away.
Find one and name it quietly, the way the troubled ones were named all week. Let it be as small as it is; small still counts.

wordCard.voice: Sobhana. Beautiful: the manual's name for the factors that color a moment well. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali sobhana: beautiful, the manual's name for the factors on the bright side.

carryVoice: Your line: the beautiful. Faith, care and an open hand, each one a moment. A week of factors, done.
